summary.title: Linux Productivity Tools (LISA19 tutorial slides)
summary.one_liner: A slide-deck tutorial teaching Bash command-line productivity: core Linux commands, navigation and history shortcuts, wildcards, and I/O redirection.
takeaways: Bash shortcuts (ctrl-a/ctrl-e, ctrl-w, ctrl-u, ctrl-y, ctrl-r) speed up editing and history recall.
History expansion such as !!, !$ and !* reuses previous commands and arguments.
Wildcards (*, ?, [!...]) expand at runtime, and quoting or escaping prevents expansion.
Standard streams are file descriptors 0, 1 and 2, and angle-bracket operators (>, >>, <, <<) redirect them.
Tools for inspecting the system, processes, files and downloads (lscpu, free, ps, nice, cat/less, diff, curl/wget, lynx) are covered.
summary.summary: This is a LISA19 (October 2019) slide deck by Ketan M. of Oak Ridge National Laboratory on Linux productivity at the command line, targeting Bash with default key bindings on GNU/Linux. The deck's outline lists parts on basics, streams and redirection, classic tools (find, grep, awk, sed), tmux, ssh config and tunneling, Bash tools, and miscellaneous utilities. The portion provided covers the overview, system and process inspection, manual and help lookup, file viewing and comparison, command-line downloads, line-editing and history shortcuts, wildcards, and I/O stream redirection. It is presented as short examples and slide bullets, with practice data files offered separately.
